sections.title: F Tool Use Capabilities of Pretrained SSMs

abstract_sentences.text: State Space Models (SSMs) have become the leading alternative to Transformers for sequence modeling tasks.
Their primary advantage is efficiency in long-context and long-form generation, enabled by fixed-size memory and linear scaling of computational complexity.

We begin this work by showing a simple theoretical result stating that SSMs cannot accurately solve any “truly long-form” generation problem (in a sense we formally define), undermining their main competitive advantage.

evidence.anchor: cannot accurately solve any “truly long-form” generation problem

abstract_sentences.text: However, we show that this limitation can be mitigated by allowing SSMs interactive access to external tools.

In fact, we show that given the right choice of tool access and problem-dependent training data, SSMs can learn to solve any tractable problem and generalize to arbitrary problem length/complexity (i.e., achieve length generalization).

evidence.anchor: given the right choice of tool access and problem-dependent training data

abstract_sentences.text: Following our theoretical finding, we demonstrate that tool-augmented SSMs achieve remarkable length generalization on a variety of arithmetic, reasoning, and coding tasks.
These findings highlight SSMs as a potential efficient alternative to Transformers in interactive tool-based and agentic settings.

experimental_design.name: research-question ordering
experimental_design.description: Section 3 orders arithmetic, algorithmic/reasoning, coding, then long-context natural language, matching the introduction’s mechanism-to-application progression. No preregistered hypotheses are listed.

experimental_design.name: interactive trajectory protocol
experimental_design.description: Models interleave thoughts, output/final-answer tokens and commands followed by environmental observations, in the ReAct-style framework defined in Section 2.

experimental_design.name: synthetic arithmetic protocol
experimental_design.description: Pointer-based memory supports new pointers, one-token left/right moves and reads. Training uses teacher forcing/next-token prediction, masking the question and read observations; evaluation uses exact trajectory plus final-answer recovery.

evidence.anchor: standard next-token prediction objective with teacher-forcing
exact-recovery of the trajectory and the final answer

experimental_design.name: algorithmic/reasoning protocol
experimental_design.description: Hanoi uses pointer memory and exact valid-move sequences; logical graph has k=3 input nodes and a search tool that returns all matching context lines.

evidence.anchor: a search tool: the model can issue a command find(x)

experimental_design.name: coding protocol
experimental_design.description: Synthetic Python dependency graphs have n=4–16 files/functions and a v10 propagation bug. Three trajectory generators are used; only correct and shorter-than-average trajectories are retained before 1.4B Mamba/Pythia finetuning.

evidence.anchor: filter the trajectories to include only trajectories that correctly fixed the code

experimental_design.name: natural-language protocol
experimental_design.description: A representative Oolong task built from Yahoo Answers examples trains on datasets of at most 5 examples and evaluates to 25 with a retrieval-next-example tool.

experimental_design.name: architectures and baselines
experimental_design.description: Synthetic runs compare Mamba-130M, LSTM, GRU, Pythia-160M, and a scaled Mistral-style local-attention Transformer. Mamba/Pythia share 24 layers, 768-d model size and 1536-d intermediate size; the Mistral-style baseline has 8 layers.

experimental_design.name: optimization and hardware
experimental_design.description: Synthetic runs sweep learning rate, batch size and weight decay for 2,000 steps with 2 seeds and report the best model. Code finetunes use a fixed setting for 200 steps; all experiments use one node with 8 H100 GPUs.

final_judgment.single_storyline: A finite-memory GSSM cannot cover unbounded long-form outputs when it only reasons or makes one tool call; multi-turn external read/write state changes the information interface so a finite controller can execute local Turing-style transitions. The experimental tasks instantiate pointer, search and bash versions of that mechanism.
final_judgment.single_storyline_evidence: PDF p.5–6, “bounded memory” and “both necessary and sufficient”; PDF p.17, “The oracle O accepts”.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the long-form/GSSM/tool-regime definitions, theorem statements, compact pointer mechanism, task protocols, Table 1 and Figures 1–3. It places proofs and extensive robustness evidence elsewhere.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps_evidence: PDF p.4–10; p.6 directs proofs to Appendix B and p.7–8 directs ablations to D.6–D.9.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A/B carry the protocol and proof; C carries architecture/sweep; D carries exact algorithms, seed variation and ablations; E carries the coding prompt; F carries BFCL. Appendix length is roughly 0.95 of readable main-body text.

final_judgment.best_pattern: Front-load a visible mechanism/result pair, follow with adjacent negative and positive formal theorems, then place a compact cross-task result table immediately before experimental detail.
final_judgment.best_pattern_evidence: PDF p.2–3, Figures 1–2; p.6, Theorems 2.1–2.2; p.7, Table 1.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The positive theorem is a constructed, task-specific trace result for a finite string-matching learner and particular oracle, while the empirical Mamba evidence is finite, mostly synthetic, success-conditioned in coding, and lacks a direct end-to-end efficiency comparison.
final_judgment.largest_gap_evidence: PDF p.6 footnote 6; p.9 filtering paragraph; p.19 seed/best-model statement; p.10 conclusion.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a tool-mediated capability claim, expose the no-tool impossibility boundary, name the changed information state, give an executable local trajectory, and test the matching component ablation at OOD lengths with a stated metric.
final_judgment.transfer_rule_evidence: PDF p.5–6 protocol/theorems; p.24–25 D.7; p.7 Table 1.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule applies when tool state, protocol and training trajectories can be specified. It does not establish tool selection, noisy-environment robustness or lower end-to-end cost for open real-agent work.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary_evidence: PDF p.6 theorem assumptions; p.9 synthetic coding construction; p.27 pretrained SSM availability note.
